exposure: place of birth (private vs. government hospital)
maternal employment status (staying at home vs. employed)
cohort: Mothers with infants aged below six months, with a mean age of 28.49 years, recruited from outpatient settings of two secondary care hospitals in the Delhi-National Capital Region, India.
finding: The study estimated the prevalence of possible postpartum depression at 18.28%, with C-section, husband's alcohol consumption, and giving birth in private hospitals significantly increasing the odds, and being a stay-at-home mother, having no specific preference for the newborn's gender, and living in nuclear families significantly lowering the odds.
mod_finding: Mothers who underwent C-section had significantly higher odds of having PPD (adjusted odds ratio, 4.39; 95% CI, 1.02-18.85).
cross-section timing: When infants were aged below six months
